instruction: I ordered a EKET Cabinet on amazon for my friend, Carl, this week, but they don't want it anymore. Initiate a return for it and forward email confirmation containing the return label to them. They live near USPS so it'll be easy for them to drop it.
notes: Three-app task: amazon (find this week's EKET Cabinet order and product, look up the USPS deliverer id, initiate a quantity-1 return), phone (search contacts for Carl's email address), gmail (locate the auto-generated 'Amazon Return Confirmation and Label' email and forward it from its thread to Carl). Initiating the return is what creates the confirmation email, so gmail-show-inbox-threads requires (return-initiated-for ?o). Forwarding via forward_email_from_thread yields the required 'Fwd: ...' subject, response_to_email_id link, and order-id in the body. Static init facts (order-query, ordered-product, contact-query, confirmation-thread, in-thread, has-email) encode which lookups reveal which entities; known-id/known-email are the knowledge predicates gating downstream calls. supervisor-complete-task takes the task-record objects (not API arguments) so its precondition mirrors the goal; it is forced last via (not (task-completed)) on every other action. Addresses, cart and payment cards are never touched, matching the evaluation's unchanged-model constraints.
